title: Transient spike sandbox: latency vs cost probe
body:
Purpose:
Quick sandbox notes from a small set of spike experiments aimed at understanding short transient surges (1–30s) and the immediate latency vs. marginal cost tradeoffs. This is rough — experiments ran on a dev pool (g5.2x) with synthetic traffic generator (bursty Poisson + sine-envelope). Not production-grade but useful to sketch heuristics for SLO-aware fallbacks.

Background / motivation:
- Observed customer incidents where a sudden 20x short-duration QPS bump (~10–25s) drove p99 from 420ms -> 2.1s while average token cost shot up 3x due to inefficient packing and cold KV misses.
- Need simple knobs / policies to trade small, acceptable p99 increases for large, predictable cost savings during spikes.

Experiment matrix (high level):
- Baseline: on-demand fastpath, smallbatch (batch size target 4), KV cache cold at start (0% hits).
- Prefetch-mode: proactive preallocation + warm KV (simulate 70% hits).
- Slotized-mode: reserve fixed slots (low packing efficiency) but predictable tail.
- Hybrid: opportunistic tiling + quick-fallback to smaller model (quantized) on sustained tail > 15s.

Key metrics captured:
- p50/p90/p95/p99 latency (ms)
- tokens-per-second served (throughput)
- marginal GPU $ per 1k queries (approx)
- KV cache hit rate (%)
- average tokens-per-batch

Text-table: selected runs (synthetic 60s window with a 15s spike to 12x baseline)

Mode           | KV-hit | avg batch | p50(ms) | p95(ms) | p99(ms) | thpt (t/s) | $/1k q | notes
---------------|--------|-----------|---------|---------|---------|-----------|--------|--------------------------------
Baseline        | 12%    | 3.8       | 110     | 560     | 2100    | 18        | 2.6    | high p99, cold-start burst pain
Prefetch-mode   | 72%    | 5.4       | 95      | 320     | 680     | 24        | 3.2    | better p99, higher cost due to reserved warm capacity
Slotized-mode   | 40%    | 2.1       | 160     | 780     | 1100    | 12        | 1.8    | cost-efficient, throughput drops, more avg latency
Hybrid          | 65%    | 4.2       | 120     | 420     | 750     | 20        | 2.1    | stable tail, graceful quantized fallback kicks in at 15s

Interpretation notes:
- Prefetch-mode reduces p99 dramatically for short spikes but increases steady marginal cost (warm resources + wasted cycles). Good for customers who value p99 strongly for even short bursts.
- Slotized-mode is cheapest per-query but hurts throughput and shifts latency curve left: increased p50/p90 but lower cost. Could be ok for asynchronous workloads.
- Hybrid offers a middle ground: keep a modest warm footprint, fall back to a quantized variant after 12–18s of sustained elevated tail. This produced a consistent reduction in cost (~20% vs Prefetch) while keeping p99 < 800ms in our probe.

Small ASCII sparkline (p99 over time; X-axis = 60s window, Y ~ 0–2200ms):
[   80s] | baseline:  __/^^^\______^^^\______/^^^^^\__  (peaks near 2100ms during spike)
         | prefetch : __/^^\_____\^______\^____ (peaks ~680ms)
         | slotized : ___/^^^^^\__________^^^^ (sustain higher med latency but lower tail)
         | hybrid   : __/^^^\_____^^\_____^^\_ (keeps tail bounded)

Quick sensitivity slices (p99 vs KV-hit % at fixed 12x spike):
- 10% KV-hit -> p99 ~ 2000ms (baseline smallbatches)
- 40% KV-hit -> p99 ~ 1100ms
- 70% KV-hit -> p99 ~ 700ms
- 90% KV-hit -> p99 ~ 420ms
Implication: KV pre-warming yields nonlinear improvements for p99 for transient spikes. Small investment in targeted prefetching (top 200 intents) can pay off.

Cost framing (back-of-envelope):
- We approximate GPU runtime $ at $0.12/vGPU-second (dev price). Under baseline burst, effective token inefficiency + cold starts adds ~0.7s extra GPU time per query on p99 tail -> ~ $0.084 per query extra during spike.
- Slotized-mode trades latency for a ~30–40% reduction in per-query GPU time during peak (less context-switching, lower kernel churn).

Operational ideas to test next (actionable):
1) Intent-aware mini-prefetch: maintain a tiny LRU of hottest user-intents and pre-warm KV + prefix cache when a session enters a known intent. Measure hit lift and incremental cost. (Ticket: JIRA-REINF-372)
2) Burst-duration thresholding: if high p99 persists >12s, auto-fallback to quantized model variant for that session (track quality regression with a small eval set).
3) Adaptive slot share: dynamically resize reserved slot fraction during the first 30s of a spike then decay to 0 over 60s — tune for 80th percentile spike lengths.
4) Expose a customer policy: "spike-mode: conservative|balanced|aggressive" that maps to prefetch size + fallback thresholds.

Open questions / caveats:
- Synthetic traffic may underrepresent multimodal token mixes (multimodal and long-context queries inflate compute per token). Need to re-run with sampled org traces (privacy-safe) to calibrate.
- QoE impact of quantized fallback requires human eval or reference dev signals; some tasks saw subtle hallucination changes in quick checks.
- Cost numbers here use dev GPU pricing; extrapolation to Dedicated pools will change break-even points.

Short next steps (who/what):
- Diego: run a 6-hour trace-replay for 3 customers (sanitized) with hybrid policy and log p99/kvcache/quality deltas (JIRA-REINF-388).
- Priya: prototype an LRU intent-prefetcher in the runtime (small config toggle) and measure hit improvement on dev pool.
- Ava: synth a slide with the tables + ASCII sparklines and call out customer policy proposal for product review next week.

Notes-to-self (fragment):
- Consider measuring kernel switch overhead separately (kernel-launch count per request). Might be the hidden cost during microbursts.
- Are there cheap HW-prefetch primitives on our infra partners (NVIDIA MIG tuning)? Follow up with infra owners.

End of sandbox dump. This is intentionally terse and exploratory — aim is to incubate 1–2 simple runtime features that give predictable tail control with observable cost anchors.
